fields.headline: PARAVISION WINS UP TO $6.5M DEAL
fields.deck: Records do not say which Paravision products were bought.

stories.caption:
The State Department has given facial recognition firm Paravision an award worth up to $6.5 million, based on federal procurement records. The records label the work "digital detection/identity assurance."

The department signed the award on September 23 and committed $1.3 million at the start. The firm-fixed-price contract runs through September 22, 2031. It was competed under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and only one offer came in.

Public award records do not say which Paravision products the department is buying. The description lines up with deepfake detection and liveness detection tools that Paravision sells to flag manipulated and AI-generated faces, but the records do not confirm whether either is included.

Separately, the department made a $24,717 purchase on April 30 for a software license. Records do not show whether that buy was a trial or a step toward the larger contract.

Source: Biometric Update, 17OCT26

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, across U.S. waters.

Why: Operating without a crew lets the vessels hold station where crewed patrols are costly or unsafe.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels deployed in the Gulf of America for U.S. maritime border security, expanding work on the Rio Grande since January 2026, per Seasats.

Seasats announced Oct. 2, 2026 that a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels has been deployed in support of U.S. maritime border security. The vessels launch from the Texas coast and conduct persistent autonomous surveillance, building on earlier support of Operation River Wall along the southern border.

Each Lightfish is roughly 11 feet long and 340 pounds, solar powered, and built for multi-month endurance on station. Seasats says two people can launch and recover one from a boat ramp or a pickup truck bed.

The company says the Homeland Defense work is part of a wider effort to close maritime surveillance gaps that depend heavily on crewed aircraft and boats, and the Assistant Secretary of War for Homeland Defense and Americas Security Affairs, Mark R Ditlevson, called industry partners such as Seasats part of efforts to secure the nation's maritime domain.

fields.headline: XTEND TO BUILD 6,000 STRIKERS FOR $40.5M
fields.deck: The company says it advances to Gauntlet III after its Gauntlet II result.

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics (NYSE: XTND) has won a $40.5 million order for 6,000 STRIKER systems. The award follows the company's placement among the top performers in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Gauntlet II, part of the U.S. Department of War's Drone Dominance Program, a $1 billion iterative effort. The company also released preliminary third quarter 2026 revenue and an update on its backlog.

STRIKER runs on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is built for tactical work in confined, complex and GNSS-denied settings. XTEND's CEO, Aviv Shapira, said the company "competed," "proved our capabilities," and is now "ready to build."

Under the program's structure, Gauntlet II top performers move straight to Gauntlet III in the mission set where they were selected, but only after filling a 400-system production order. Results in Gauntlet III will decide whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and the company notes that taking part does not guarantee an award.

Source: BUSINESS WIRE, 13OCT26

MISSION BRIEF // SKYDIO X10D

//Skydio

📍San Mateo, CA

Tech: Contested-environment resilience

Platform: Small UAS (sUAS)

Goal: Keep small drones flying for reconnaissance when GPS and communications are jammed.

Why: Vision-based navigation and anchor points let the drone return and navigate where satellite positioning is denied.

Private company → Backers: Not stated in source.

Traction: Listed on the Blue UAS Cleared list, per Skydio.

The Skydio X10D is a small unmanned aircraft that the company says delivers electronic warfare resilience and survivability. According to Skydio's product page, it can switch channels on a multiband radio, use Visual Inertial Odometry at altitudes up to several kilometers in GNSS-denied or spoofed environments, and navigate with Anchor Points in GPS-denied conditions. It is IP55 rated against dust and water, with a stated maximum speed of 45 mph and deployment time under 40 seconds.

The page also lists NightSense, which uses visible or infrared illumination for obstacle avoidance and navigation in zero-light conditions, and VT300-Z and VT300-L sensor packages with narrow, telephoto and thermal cameras. Skydio states that the drone is NDAA compliant and fully offline, with AES 256 encrypted links.

These are manufacturer specifications from the product page, not independent test results. The page does not state a publication date or specific fielding units.

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE TECH IN AFRICA
fields.deck: Soldiers will test systems in Morocco and aim to field them within 180 days.

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) is working with the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to run tests in Africa, with the goal of getting proven systems to Soldiers inside six months.

The first accelerated capability event (ACE) is set for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It targets counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, with a focus on shielding early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. The Army says Africa's open spectrum, lightly used airspace and varied terrain let Soldiers prove solutions in theater before scaling them across the service.

The ACE runs in three phases: submission and preparation, Soldier-led demonstrations, and follow-on operational evaluation. SETAF-AF plans a Soldier-led demonstration in February and March 2027, then an operational assessment in April and May during African Lion 2027. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, October 16, 2026

stories.caption:
Three MilCityUSA stories from the past week, with the cards as they were published.

Microchip Technology acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and its HARDSIL process technology to its space and defense portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge for the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

The Florida National Guard ran Drone Crucible 26.3, an integration test at Camp Blanding, Sept. 26 to Oct. 2, linking drone, targeting and video data into one shared picture.

Source: Microchip Technology, Oct. 9, 2026; Lockheed Martin, Oct. 9, 2026; Florida National Guard report via army.mil, Oct. 6, 2026.
